name: Distal Radioulnar Joint Instability
definition: Pathological instability of the distal radioulnar joint, often after trauma, TFCC injury or malunited distal radius fracture.

investigations.principle: Radiographs and CT assess alignment; MRI evaluates TFCC and soft tissues.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, physeal, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Persistent structural instability may require TFCC repair or corrective reconstruction.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Manibandha-Sandhi instability phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Pathological instability of the distal radioulnar joint, often after trauma, TFCC injury or malunited distal radius fracture.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, open injury, severe deformity, rapidly progressive neurological symptoms, suspected infection or other listed red flags.
